topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The chairman gave a (brief) speech.
topic_questions.explanation: Brief means short or lasting for a short time.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The man's explanation was (ambiguous).
topic_questions.explanation: Ambiguous means unclear or open to more than one interpretation, so clear is its opposite.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Neither the teacher nor the students _____ aware of the change.
topic_questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'students', which is plural.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The committee decided to _____ the meeting until Monday.
topic_questions.explanation: Postpone means to delay an event until a later time.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The witness gave a (credible) account of the incident.
topic_questions.explanation: Credible means believable or worthy of being trusted.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If I _____ about the meeting, I would have attended it.
topic_questions.explanation: The sentence describes an unreal past condition, so 'had known' is required.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The medicine had an (adverse) effect on the patient.
topic_questions.explanation: Adverse means harmful or unfavorable, while beneficial means helpful or favorable.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The students were warned against _____ during the examination.
topic_questions.explanation: The preposition 'against' is followed by a gerund, so 'cheating' is correct.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The manager (commended) the workers for their dedication.
topic_questions.explanation: Commended means praised or expressed approval of someone.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She has lived in Lagos _____ 2022.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time such as 2022.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Musa is one of the players who _____ regularly for the team.
topic_questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural noun 'players', so 'train' is correct.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The instructions were (mandatory).
topic_questions.explanation: Mandatory means required, while optional means left to personal choice.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The new policy will (mitigate) the problem.
topic_questions.explanation: Mitigate means to make something less severe or reduce its effect.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: I prefer reading novels _____ watching television.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct construction is 'prefer something to something else'.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The man's statement was (deliberate).
topic_questions.explanation: Deliberate means intentional or done on purpose, while accidental means unintentional.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: By the time we arrived, the film _____.
topic_questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had started' shows that the film began before another past event.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The student was (diligent) in his studies.
topic_questions.explanation: Diligent means hardworking and careful in one's efforts.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The police are investigating the cause _____ the accident.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct expression is 'the cause of the accident'.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The evidence was (scarce).
topic_questions.explanation: Scarce means insufficient or difficult to obtain, while abundant means plentiful.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Each of the candidates _____ required to present an identification card.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and therefore takes the singular verb 'is'.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The old building was (demolished).
topic_questions.explanation: Demolished means pulled down or destroyed, especially in reference to a building.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She is accustomed to _____ early every morning.
topic_questions.explanation: The expression 'accustomed to' is followed by a noun or gerund, so 'waking' is correct.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The chairman was (optimistic) about the project.
topic_questions.explanation: Optimistic means hopeful about the future, while doubtful expresses uncertainty or lack of confidence.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The man _____ car was stolen reported the matter to the police.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Whose' is used to indicate possession and correctly relates the car to the man.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The speaker's argument was (coherent).
topic_questions.explanation: Coherent means logical, consistent and easy to understand.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Hardly had the match begun _____ it started to rain.
topic_questions.explanation: The standard construction is 'hardly...when'.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The proposal is (feasible).
topic_questions.explanation: Feasible means possible or practical, while impossible means unable to be done.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The children enjoyed _____ at the party.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct plural reflexive pronoun referring to 'children' is 'themselves'.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The achievement was (remarkable).
topic_questions.explanation: Remarkable means worthy of attention or notable.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The teacher asked me _____ I had completed the assignment.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Whether' introduces an indirect question that requires a yes-or-no answer.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The man was (generous) to the poor.
topic_questions.explanation: Generous means willing to give freely, while selfish describes someone unwilling to share.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The books on the table _____ mine.
topic_questions.explanation: The subject 'books' is plural, so the correct verb is 'are'.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The government plans to (eradicate) the disease.
topic_questions.explanation: Eradicate means to completely remove or destroy something.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The woman _____ I met yesterday is a doctor.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Whom' is used as the object of the verb 'met' when referring to a person.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The road was (narrow).
topic_questions.explanation: The opposite of narrow is wide.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: We must comply _____ the instructions given by the authorities.
topic_questions.explanation: The verb 'comply' is followed by the preposition 'with'.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The athlete was (exhausted) after the race.
topic_questions.explanation: Exhausted means extremely tired.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The students have been waiting _____ two hours.
topic_questions.explanation: 'For' is used to indicate a period or duration of time.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The child was (obedient) to his parents.
topic_questions.explanation: Obedient means willing to follow instructions, while disobedient means unwilling to do so.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The principal, together with the teachers, _____ attending the ceremony.
topic_questions.explanation: The main subject is the singular noun 'principal'; the phrase 'together with the teachers' does not change its number.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The company decided to (terminate) the contract.
topic_questions.explanation: Terminate means to bring something to an end.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: I wish I _____ taller.
topic_questions.explanation: For an unreal present situation after 'I wish', 'were' is the appropriate form.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The instructions were (explicit).
topic_questions.explanation: Explicit means clearly stated, while vague means unclear or lacking precise details.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The farmer prevented the goats _____ entering the garden.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct construction is 'prevent someone or something from doing something'.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The witness gave a (vague) description of the suspect.
topic_questions.explanation: Vague means unclear or lacking precise details.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The news _____ surprising to everyone present.
topic_questions.explanation: 'News' is treated as a singular uncountable noun, so it takes 'was'.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The man's excuse was (plausible).
topic_questions.explanation: Plausible means seemingly reasonable or believable, while unlikely expresses the opposite idea.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The students arrived at the hall _____ time for the examination.
topic_questions.explanation: The expression 'in time' means early enough to meet a required deadline or event.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The manager considered the plan (prudent).
topic_questions.explanation: Prudent means wise and careful, especially when making decisions.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If she had studied harder, she _____ the examination.
topic_questions.explanation: A third conditional sentence uses 'would have' followed by the past participle.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in brackets: The water in the container was (abundant).
topic_questions.explanation: Abundant means plentiful, while scarce means insufficient or limited.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The boy succeeded _____ solving the difficult problem.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct expression is 'succeed in doing something'.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in brackets: The teacher gave an (accurate) account of the event.
topic_questions.explanation: Accurate means correct or exact.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The students were asked to submit _____ assignments before noon.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Their' is the possessive determiner required before the noun 'assignments'.

topic_questions.text:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows.

A young entrepreneur started a small food business from home. At first, she had only a few customers, but she paid close attention to their comments. She improved the quality of her products, introduced new varieties and ensured that orders were delivered on time. Gradually, satisfied customers recommended the business to others. Within a year, the number of customers had increased considerably.

What was the most important source of new customers mentioned in the passage?
topic_questions.explanation: The passage states that satisfied customers recommended the business to others, bringing in new customers.

topic_questions.text:
Read the passage and answer the question that follows.

A young entrepreneur started a small food business from home. At first, she had only a few customers, but she paid close attention to their comments. She improved the quality of her products, introduced new varieties and ensured that orders were delivered on time. Gradually, satisfied customers recommended the business to others. Within a year, the number of customers had increased considerably.

Which quality of the entrepreneur is most clearly demonstrated in the passage?
topic_questions.explanation: The entrepreneur listened to customer comments and made improvements to her products and services, showing a willingness to improve.

topic_questions.text: The students were advised to ____ their assignments before submitting them.
topic_questions.explanation: After 'to', the base form of the verb 'review' is required.

topic_questions.text: Although the road was flooded, the driver ____ to reach the village.
topic_questions.explanation: The past tense 'refused' agrees with the past context of the sentence.

topic_questions.text: The principal congratulated the students ____ their excellent performance.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct expression is 'congratulated someone on something'.

topic_questions.text: If Musa had arrived earlier, he ____ the beginning of the examination.
topic_questions.explanation: A past unreal condition takes 'would have' plus the past participle.

topic_questions.text: The manager asked the workers to be ____ because the meeting would begin shortly.
topic_questions.explanation: The adjective 'patient' is needed after 'be'.

topic_questions.text: Neither the teacher nor the students ____ aware of the change in timetable.
topic_questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'students', which is plural.

topic_questions.text: The farmer harvested his crops ____ the rainy season began.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Before' correctly shows that the harvesting happened earlier than the rainy season.

topic_questions.text: The boy was punished because he had ____ the school rules.
topic_questions.explanation: The past participle 'broken' is required after 'had'.

topic_questions.text: The new library provides students ____ enough space to study quietly.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct expression is 'provide someone with something'.

topic_questions.text: She speaks English ____ than her younger sister.
topic_questions.explanation: The comparative adverb 'more fluently' is used to compare two people.

topic_questions.text: The villagers were worried because the river had ____ its banks.
topic_questions.explanation: The past participle of 'burst' is 'burst', so 'had burst' is correct.

topic_questions.text: The chairman insisted ____ seeing the original document.
topic_questions.explanation: The verb 'insist' is followed by the preposition 'on'.

topic_questions.text: The children were excited ____ the announcement of the school trip.
topic_questions.explanation: The natural expression is 'excited about something'.

topic_questions.text: By the time we arrived, the film ____ already started.
topic_questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had started' shows that the film began before our arrival.

topic_questions.text: The doctor advised the patient to take the medicine ____.
topic_questions.explanation: The adverb 'regularly' modifies the verb 'take'.

topic_questions.text: The woman could not enter the hall because she had ____ her ticket at home.
topic_questions.explanation: The past participle 'left' is required after 'had'.

topic_questions.text: The teacher was pleased ____ the students' improvement.
topic_questions.explanation: The adjective 'pleased' is commonly followed by 'with' when referring to something that satisfies someone.

topic_questions.text: The athlete trained hard ____ he could win the competition.
topic_questions.explanation: 'So that' introduces the purpose of the athlete's training.

topic_questions.text: The police are looking ____ the cause of the accident.
topic_questions.explanation: The phrasal expression 'look into' means to investigate.

topic_questions.text: The teacher asked the pupils ____ they had completed the exercise.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Whether' is appropriate when introducing an indirect yes-or-no question.

topic_questions.text: The company will employ more workers if its profits ____ next year.
topic_questions.explanation: In the first conditional, the 'if' clause takes the simple present tense.

topic_questions.text: The child was too tired ____ any further.
topic_questions.explanation: The structure 'too + adjective + to + verb' requires 'to walk'.

topic_questions.text: The secretary is responsible ____ keeping the records of the organisation.
topic_questions.explanation: The adjective 'responsible' is followed by the preposition 'for'.

topic_questions.text: The farmer bought a new machine because it would make his work ____.
topic_questions.explanation: The comparative adjective 'easier' describes the effect of the machine on his work.

topic_questions.text: Hardly had the bell rung ____ the students rushed out of the classroom.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct correlative structure is 'hardly...when'.

topic_questions.text: The woman was accused ____ stealing money from the office.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct expression is 'accused of' something.

topic_questions.text: The boys decided to postpone the match ____ the heavy rain.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Because of' is followed by a noun phrase and correctly gives the reason for postponing the match.

topic_questions.text: The speaker spoke so quietly that nobody could ____ him clearly.
topic_questions.explanation: After the modal 'could', the base form 'hear' is required.

topic_questions.text: The two friends have known each other ____ childhood.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific starting point in time such as 'childhood'.

topic_questions.text: The committee has ____ its decision after several hours of discussion.
topic_questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has made' requires the past participle 'made'.

topic_questions.text: The student was absent ____ he was suffering from malaria.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Because' introduces the reason for the student's absence.

topic_questions.text: The workers were asked to arrive ____ time for the ceremony.
topic_questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'on time', meaning at the scheduled time.

topic_questions.text: The old bridge is no longer safe, so the government plans to ____ it.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Replace' fits the context because an unsafe bridge is to be removed and substituted with another.

topic_questions.text: The teacher warned the students not to ____ noise during the examination.
topic_questions.explanation: The standard expression is 'make noise'.

topic_questions.text: The young man succeeded ____ his parents' expectations.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct structure is 'succeed in' followed by a gerund, 'meeting'.

topic_questions.text: The manager will attend the conference ____ he receives permission from the director.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces a condition that must be fulfilled.

topic_questions.text: The woman was very tired, but she continued ____ until the work was completed.
topic_questions.explanation: The verb 'continued' can be followed by the gerund 'working' in this context.

topic_questions.text: The boy apologized ____ his teacher for arriving late.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct expression is 'apologized to someone for something'.

topic_questions.text: The farmer has planted enough maize to ____ his family for several months.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Feed his family' is the most appropriate expression in this context.

topic_questions.text: The examination was difficult, but most candidates ____ to answer the questions correctly.
topic_questions.explanation: The past tense 'managed' agrees with the past context.

topic_questions.text: The principal asked the prefects to ensure that the classrooms were kept ____.
topic_questions.explanation: The adjective 'clean' describes the condition in which the classrooms should be kept.

topic_questions.text: The man would have won the race if he ____ harder.
topic_questions.explanation: A third conditional requires 'if + past perfect', so 'had trained' is correct.

topic_questions.text: The students were prevented ____ entering the laboratory without permission.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct structure is 'prevented from doing something'.

topic_questions.text: The woman bought a new dress ____ she could wear it to the wedding.
topic_questions.explanation: 'So that' correctly expresses the purpose of buying the dress.

topic_questions.text: The teacher said that the examination would begin as soon as the candidates ____ seated.
topic_questions.explanation: In reported speech with a past reporting verb, 'were' correctly agrees with the plural subject 'candidates'.

topic_questions.text: The committee was divided ____ the best way to solve the problem.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Divided about' is appropriate when people disagree over an issue.

topic_questions.text: The student worked hard and was eventually ____ for his efforts.
topic_questions.explanation: The passive construction 'was rewarded' requires the past participle 'rewarded'.

topic_questions.text: The road was closed ____ the heavy flooding in the area.
topic_questions.explanation: 'Because of' correctly introduces the noun phrase giving the reason for the closure.

topic_questions.text: The children were told to keep ____ while the visitors were speaking.
topic_questions.explanation: The adjective 'quiet' describes the state the children were expected to maintain.

topic_questions.text: The director congratulated the staff ____ completing the project successfully.
topic_questions.explanation: The correct expression is 'congratulated someone on doing something'.

topic_questions.text: The farmer could not sell his produce because the market had ____ before he arrived.
topic_questions.explanation: The past participle 'closed' is required after 'had'.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The manager turned a deaf ear to the workers' complaints' mean?
options: The manager listened carefully to the workers
The manager refused to pay attention to the workers' complaints
The manager became deaf after hearing the complaints
The manager asked the workers to speak louder
topic_questions.explanation: To turn a deaf ear means to deliberately refuse to listen or pay attention.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'Ngozi is in hot water over the missing documents' mean?
options: Ngozi is in a difficult or troublesome situation
Ngozi is working near a hot-water tank
Ngozi has found the missing documents
topic_questions.explanation: Being in hot water means being in trouble or facing difficulties.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The chairman called the meeting off' mean?
options: The chairman ended or cancelled the meeting
The chairman invited everyone to the meeting
The chairman postponed his speech until the meeting
The chairman attended the meeting late
topic_questions.explanation: To call something off means to cancel it.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The boy took to his heels when he saw the police' mean?
options: The boy stood still before the police
The boy asked the police for help
topic_questions.explanation: To take to one's heels means to run away quickly.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The new policy has come under fire' mean?
options: The policy has been praised by everyone
The policy has attracted strong criticism
The policy has been withdrawn from use
The policy has been explained to the public
topic_questions.explanation: To come under fire means to receive strong criticism.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The witness gave a convincing account of the incident' mean?
options: The witness gave an unbelievable story
The witness refused to describe the incident
The witness gave an account that was difficult to understand
The witness gave a believable and persuasive description
topic_questions.explanation: A convincing account is one that is believable and persuasive.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The student barely passed the examination' mean?
options: The student passed with an excellent score
The student failed the examination completely
The student passed by a very small margin
The student did not take the examination
topic_questions.explanation: Barely passed means passed with only a small margin above the required mark.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The principal is highly regarded by the staff' mean?
options: The staff strongly dislike the principal
The staff respect the principal greatly
The staff rarely see the principal
The staff have never met the principal
topic_questions.explanation: To be highly regarded means to be greatly respected or admired.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The politician's promise was merely a storm in a teacup' mean?
options: The promise caused a major national crisis
The promise was made during a storm
The issue appeared more serious than it really was
The politician refused to make any promise
topic_questions.explanation: A storm in a teacup refers to a small issue that has been made to seem very serious.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The workers were asked to keep an eye on the equipment' mean?
options: They were asked to repair the equipment
They were asked to watch the equipment carefully
They were asked to sell the equipment
They were asked to move the equipment outside
topic_questions.explanation: To keep an eye on something means to watch or monitor it carefully.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The witness changed his story at the eleventh hour' mean?
options: He changed his story very early
He changed his story at the last possible moment
He repeated his story several times
He refused to tell his story
topic_questions.explanation: At the eleventh hour means at the last possible moment.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The teacher's explanation shed light on the problem' mean?
options: The explanation made the problem more confusing
The explanation made the problem clearer
topic_questions.explanation: To shed light on something means to make it clearer or easier to understand.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The two companies are at loggerheads over the contract' mean?
options: The companies are working together happily
The companies are competing in the same market
The companies are in serious disagreement
The companies have signed the contract
topic_questions.explanation: To be at loggerheads means to be in strong disagreement.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The candidate has a bright future ahead of her' mean?
options: She is expected to have a successful future
She will work only during the day
She plans to travel abroad immediately
She has already completed her career
topic_questions.explanation: A bright future means one with good prospects for success.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The farmer made ends meet despite the poor harvest' mean?
options: The farmer connected the ends of two ropes
The farmer managed to live within his available income
The farmer sold all his land
The farmer borrowed money from every neighbour
topic_questions.explanation: To make ends meet means to manage one's expenses with the available income.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The new employee is still finding his feet' mean?
options: He is learning how to walk
He is looking for a new pair of shoes
He is becoming accustomed to his new situation
He has decided to leave the workplace
topic_questions.explanation: Finding one's feet means becoming familiar and comfortable with a new situation.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The announcement took everyone by surprise' mean?
topic_questions.explanation: To take someone by surprise means to surprise that person.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The governor's speech was brief but to the point' mean?
options: The speech was long and confusing
The speech was short and directly addressed the main issue
The speech contained many unrelated stories
The speech was delivered without preparation
topic_questions.explanation: A speech that is to the point deals directly and clearly with the main issue.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The company is on the verge of collapse' mean?
options: The company is very close to collapsing
The company has increased its profits
topic_questions.explanation: On the verge of something means very close to experiencing it.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The teacher's advice fell on deaf ears' mean?
options: The students listened carefully to the advice
The teacher could not hear the students
The advice was repeated several times
topic_questions.explanation: If advice falls on deaf ears, it is ignored or not acted upon.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The accused was released on bail' mean?
options: The accused was permanently freed from the case
The accused was released temporarily after providing a financial guarantee
The accused was sentenced to prison
topic_questions.explanation: Being released on bail means being temporarily released while the legal case continues, subject to conditions.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The chairman's decision was a blessing in disguise' mean?
options: The decision looked bad at first but turned out to be beneficial
The decision was clearly harmful from the beginning
The chairman regretted making the decision
topic_questions.explanation: A blessing in disguise is something that initially seems bad but later proves beneficial.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The athlete gave the competition his best shot' mean?
options: He made his greatest effort to succeed
He watched the competition from outside
He withdrew before the competition began
topic_questions.explanation: To give something one's best shot means to make one's greatest effort.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The issue is still up in the air' mean?
options: The issue has been completely resolved
The issue is being discussed outdoors
The issue has not yet been decided
topic_questions.explanation: If something is up in the air, it is uncertain or undecided.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The man is known for his generosity' mean?
options: The man is known for being very careful with money
The man is known for giving freely to others
The man is known for borrowing money
The man is known for avoiding people
topic_questions.explanation: Generosity means willingness to give or share freely.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The secretary went out of her way to help the visitor' mean?
options: She deliberately made an extra effort to help the visitor
She asked the visitor to leave immediately
She avoided speaking to the visitor
She helped the visitor only after being forced
topic_questions.explanation: To go out of one's way means to make a special or extra effort to help.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The news spread like wildfire' mean?
options: The news was reported only once
topic_questions.explanation: To spread like wildfire means to spread very quickly.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The manager has put the matter to rest' mean?
options: The manager has postponed the matter
The manager has brought the matter to an end
The manager has made the matter more difficult
The manager has hidden the matter
topic_questions.explanation: To put a matter to rest means to settle or bring it to an end.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The new law will come into effect next month' mean?
options: The law will be cancelled next month
The law will be discussed next month
The law will begin to operate next month
The law will be rewritten next month
topic_questions.explanation: To come into effect means to begin to operate or become applicable.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The student has a lot on his plate' mean?
options: He has eaten too much food
He has many tasks or responsibilities to deal with
He has lost his school materials
He has prepared food for his classmates
topic_questions.explanation: Having a lot on one's plate means having many responsibilities or tasks.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The police are trying to get to the bottom of the case' mean?
options: They want to close the case immediately
They want to discover the truth about the case
They want to ignore the evidence
They want to transfer the case to another station
topic_questions.explanation: To get to the bottom of something means to discover the truth or real cause.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The company has weathered the storm' mean?
options: The company has survived a difficult period
The company has moved to another country
The company has predicted bad weather
topic_questions.explanation: To weather the storm means to survive a difficult situation.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The two brothers are as different as chalk and cheese' mean?
options: They have exactly the same personality
They are very different from each other
They work in the same profession
topic_questions.explanation: The expression means that two people or things are extremely different.

topic_questions.text: What does the statement 'The student was caught red-handed' mean?
options: The student was caught while committing the offence
The student was wearing red clothes

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The accident was caused by the driver's carelessness.
options: The accident happened because the road was closed.
The driver's lack of care led to the accident.
The driver reported the accident to the police.
topic_questions.explanation: Carelessness means a lack of proper attention or caution.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: Despite the heavy rain, the volunteers continued distributing food to the affected families.
options: The volunteers stopped working because of the rain.
The affected families refused the food.
The rain prevented the volunteers from helping anyone.
The volunteers continued helping affected families despite the difficult weather.
topic_questions.explanation: The central point is that the volunteers continued their assistance despite the heavy rain.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The committee reached a unanimous decision.
options: All the committee members agreed on the decision.
Only the chairman supported the decision.
topic_questions.explanation: Unanimous means agreed upon by everyone involved.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The company reduced unnecessary expenses and invested more money in production, which increased its profits.
options: The company improved its profits by cutting wasteful expenses and investing in production.
The company reduced its profits by investing in production.
topic_questions.explanation: The statement explains that controlling expenses and increasing investment in production improved profits.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The old building is no longer habitable.
options: The building has recently been renovated.
The building is suitable for everyone.
The building is no longer fit for people to live in.
The building has become more comfortable.
topic_questions.explanation: Habitable means suitable or safe for living in.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The government launched a campaign to educate citizens about the dangers of improper waste disposal and encourage cleaner communities.
options: The government encouraged people to dispose of waste carelessly.
Citizens refused to participate in environmental programmes.
The government launched an educational campaign to promote proper waste disposal and cleaner communities.
topic_questions.explanation: The statement focuses on educating citizens about proper waste disposal and cleanliness.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The candidate performed exceptionally well in the interview.
options: The candidate performed extremely well in the interview.
The candidate failed to attend the interview.
The candidate performed poorly in the interview.
The candidate refused to answer the questions.
topic_questions.explanation: Exceptionally well means extremely or unusually well.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The transport company introduced additional buses during peak hours to reduce overcrowding and delays.
options: The company removed buses during busy periods.
The company added buses at busy times to reduce overcrowding and delays.
The company increased ticket prices to reduce passengers.
The company stopped operating during peak hours.
topic_questions.explanation: The main purpose of the additional buses was to reduce overcrowding and delays.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The instructions were ambiguous.
options: The instructions were easy to follow.
The instructions were unclear and could be understood in different ways.
topic_questions.explanation: Ambiguous means unclear or open to more than one interpretation.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The athlete trained consistently for several months and eventually won the competition.
options: The athlete stopped training before the competition.
The competition was cancelled after months of training.
Consistent training contributed to the athlete's eventual victory.
topic_questions.explanation: The statement links the athlete's consistent training with the eventual victory.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The chairman commended the workers for their dedication.
options: The chairman praised the workers for their commitment.
The chairman punished the workers for their mistakes.
The workers criticized the chairman's dedication.
The chairman ignored the workers' efforts.
topic_questions.explanation: To commend means to praise, while dedication means commitment to a task.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The library extended its opening hours because students needed more time to study before their examinations.
options: The library extended its hours to give students more study time.
Students refused to use the library.
The examinations were cancelled because of the library.
topic_questions.explanation: The extension of library hours was intended to provide students with more study time.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The project was completed ahead of schedule.
options: The project was cancelled before it started.
The project was finished earlier than planned.
The project was started after the deadline.
topic_questions.explanation: Ahead of schedule means completed earlier than the planned time.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The community built a health centre so that residents would have easier access to basic medical services.
options: The community closed all health centres.
The health centre was built for visitors from another town.
The community built a health centre to improve access to basic medical care.
topic_questions.explanation: The purpose of building the health centre was to make basic medical care more accessible.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The witness's testimony contradicted the evidence.
options: The witness's statement was inconsistent with the evidence.
The witness confirmed all the evidence.
The evidence was destroyed by the witness.
The witness refused to give evidence.
topic_questions.explanation: To contradict means to be inconsistent with or opposed to something.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The school organized a sanitation exercise in which students cleaned classrooms, cleared blocked drains and removed litter from the compound.
options: Students were taught only in the classrooms.
The school organized an exercise to improve cleanliness throughout the compound.
Students blocked the drains during the exercise.
The school prohibited students from cleaning.
topic_questions.explanation: The activities described all aimed at improving the cleanliness of the school environment.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The businessman was compelled to close the shop.
options: The businessman willingly opened another shop.
The businessman decided to expand his business.
The businessman was forced to close the shop.
The businessman refused to leave the shop.
topic_questions.explanation: Compelled means forced or obliged to do something.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The researchers discovered that the new method was cheaper, faster and more reliable than the old one.
options: The old method was cheaper and faster.
The researchers rejected the new method.
The two methods were exactly the same.
The researchers found the new method superior in cost, speed and reliability.
topic_questions.explanation: The statement highlights the advantages of the new method over the old one.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The teacher urged the students to take the examination seriously.
options: The teacher strongly encouraged the students to treat the examination seriously.
The teacher told the students to avoid the examination.
The teacher advised the students not to study.
topic_questions.explanation: To urge means to strongly encourage someone to do something.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: Because the market became overcrowded, the traders agreed to organize their goods in a more orderly manner.
options: The traders left the market immediately.
The crowded market led traders to improve the arrangement of their goods.
The traders made the market more crowded.
topic_questions.explanation: The main point is that overcrowding prompted the traders to organize their goods better.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The proposal was rejected on the grounds that it was too expensive.
options: The proposal was accepted because it was affordable.
The proposal was delayed because it was popular.
The proposal was turned down because its cost was too high.
The proposal was improved because it was expensive.
topic_questions.explanation: To reject means to turn down, and the reason given was its high cost.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The company provided training for its employees so they could operate the new equipment safely and efficiently.
options: The company stopped using new equipment.
The company replaced all its employees.
The company trained employees to use the new equipment safely and efficiently.
topic_questions.explanation: The purpose of the training was to ensure safe and efficient use of the new equipment.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The villagers were delighted by the arrival of the relief materials.
options: The villagers were very happy when the relief materials arrived.
The villagers rejected the relief materials.
The villagers were unaware of the relief materials.
The villagers were angry about the arrival of the materials.
topic_questions.explanation: Delighted means very happy or pleased.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The school introduced stricter examination rules to discourage cheating and maintain academic standards.
options: The school encouraged students to cheat.
The school introduced stricter rules to prevent cheating and protect academic standards.
The school removed all examination rules.
topic_questions.explanation: The purpose of the stricter rules was to discourage cheating and maintain standards.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The manager dismissed the complaint as irrelevant.
options: The manager carefully investigated the complaint.
The manager accepted the complaint as important.
The manager regarded the complaint as unrelated to the matter.
The manager apologized for the complaint.
topic_questions.explanation: Irrelevant means not related or not important to the matter being considered.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: After heavy rainfall caused flooding in several areas, the authorities evacuated residents from the most affected communities.
options: The residents caused the heavy rainfall.
The rainfall ended before any action was taken.
Flooding caused by heavy rain led authorities to evacuate residents from affected areas.
topic_questions.explanation: The main events are heavy rainfall, flooding and the evacuation of affected residents.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The speaker's argument was convincing.
options: The speaker refused to explain the argument.
topic_questions.explanation: Convincing means capable of persuading someone to accept an idea.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The farmer diversified his crops so that the failure of one crop would not cause a complete loss of income.
options: The farmer planted only one crop.
The farmer grew different crops to reduce the financial risk of crop failure.
The farmer stopped farming to protect his income.
The farmer sold all his crops before planting them.
topic_questions.explanation: Diversifying crops reduces dependence on one crop and therefore reduces financial risk.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The student was exempted from the practical examination.
options: The student was required to repeat the examination.
The student failed the practical examination.
The student was excused from taking the practical examination.
The student supervised the practical examination.
topic_questions.explanation: To be exempted means to be officially excused from a requirement.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The town's population increased rapidly after a new factory created many employment opportunities.
options: The factory reduced the town's population.
The town lost many employment opportunities.
The factory closed before workers arrived.
The availability of jobs at the new factory contributed to rapid population growth.
topic_questions.explanation: The statement connects the new employment opportunities with the town's population increase.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The doctor advised him to refrain from strenuous activities.
options: The doctor advised him to avoid physically demanding activities.
The doctor told him to exercise more intensely.
The doctor asked him to stop taking his medicine.
The doctor encouraged him to participate in competitions.
topic_questions.explanation: To refrain from means to avoid doing something, while strenuous means requiring considerable physical effort.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The local council renovated the public park, installed new lights and provided additional benches to make it more attractive and comfortable for residents.
options: The council closed the public park.
The council improved the park by adding facilities for residents' comfort.
Residents removed all the benches from the park.
The park became less attractive after renovation.
topic_questions.explanation: The renovation and added facilities were intended to improve the park for residents.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The negotiations broke down because neither side was willing to compromise.
options: The negotiations succeeded because both sides agreed.
The two sides quickly reached a settlement.
The talks failed because neither side was prepared to make concessions.
The negotiations were postponed because the venue was unavailable.
topic_questions.explanation: The negotiations broke down because both sides refused to compromise.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The school introduced a scholarship scheme to support academically strong students from disadvantaged backgrounds.
options: The school stopped supporting talented students.
Only wealthy students could receive scholarships.
The school cancelled its academic programmes.
The scholarship scheme was created to assist capable students who face financial disadvantages.
topic_questions.explanation: The scheme aims to support academically strong students who come from disadvantaged backgrounds.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The instructions were concise but comprehensive.
options: The instructions were brief but covered all the important points.
The instructions were long and incomplete.
The instructions were confusing and irrelevant.
The instructions contained no useful information.
topic_questions.explanation: Concise means brief, while comprehensive means covering all or nearly all important aspects.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The residents planted trees along the streets to provide shade, improve the appearance of the town and help protect the environment.
options: The residents removed trees from the streets.
The residents planted trees for shade, beautification and environmental benefits.
The residents wanted to reduce the number of streets.
The town became less attractive after the trees were planted.
topic_questions.explanation: The statement gives three main purposes for planting the trees: shade, beautification and environmental protection.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The company is facing an acute shortage of skilled workers.
options: The company has more skilled workers than it needs.
The company has solved its staffing problem.
The company is experiencing a serious lack of skilled workers.
The company is reducing the number of skilled workers.
topic_questions.explanation: Acute means severe or serious, while shortage means lack.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The government repaired several rural roads to make it easier for farmers to transport their produce to urban markets.
options: Farmers stopped transporting produce to cities.
Urban markets were moved to rural areas.
The government improved rural roads to facilitate the transportation of farm produce to cities.
topic_questions.explanation: The road repairs were intended to make the movement of farm produce to urban markets easier.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: His explanation was plausible.
options: His explanation was believable and reasonable.
His explanation was impossible to understand.
His explanation was unrelated to the issue.
topic_questions.explanation: Plausible means seeming reasonable or believable.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The library digitized many of its records so that students could access them more easily and quickly.
options: The library converted records into digital form to improve access.
The library prevented students from using its records.
topic_questions.explanation: Digitizing the records was done to make them easier and faster for students to access.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The chairman's remarks were inappropriate.
options: The chairman's remarks were very helpful.
The chairman's remarks were carefully prepared.
The chairman's remarks were unsuitable for the situation.
The chairman's remarks were widely appreciated.
topic_questions.explanation: Inappropriate means unsuitable or not proper for a particular situation.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best summarizes the statement: The hospital introduced an appointment system to reduce waiting time and improve the organization of patient care.
options: The hospital increased patients' waiting time.
Patients were asked to avoid making appointments.
The hospital introduced appointments to reduce delays and improve patient care.
topic_questions.explanation: The appointment system was introduced to reduce waiting and organize patient care better.

topic_questions.text: Choose the option that best paraphrases the statement: The evidence was insufficient to prove his guilt.
options: There was not enough evidence to establish that he was guilty.
The evidence proved his guilt beyond doubt.
There was no investigation into the matter.
topic_questions.explanation: Insufficient means not enough for the required purpose.
